# The kernel against made instruments, and estimates for the voicing decisions (generated by kernel_vs_references.py)

Desk numbers. Nothing here was printed or played. The reference holes are photo measurements; the estimates of sections 3 and 5 are textbook duct formulas, not models of a jet.

## 0. Which hole opens for which note

The kernel sizes each hole for the note it opens, so the order of opening decides which finger gets which diameter. Until 2026-11-18 `params/alto_c_12hole.toml` opened the left hand pinky first (A5) and the thumbs last (E6, F6); the owner then chose the Asian system, and the parameter file follows it. The Asian fingering system, the common one on 12-hole instruments, opens L ring, L middle, L index, then the left thumb (D6), the right thumb (E6) and the left pinky last (F6); the Italian system swaps the last two (Pure Ocarinas, *The ocarina's fingering system* and *Learning the ocarina's fingerings*). The low six holes open in the same order in all three.

Each instrument's measured holes were put into the kernel's scale model under each order (A4 exact, volume fitted, k_hole 1.0). *Rank* is the place of that order among all 720 ways of opening the six upper holes.

## 1. Hole by hole: three made instruments in the kernel's scale model

For each instrument: the capped air volume that brings its 13 notes closest to pitch (A4 exact, least squares over the other twelve), the error that is left on each note, and each measured hole against the hole the kernel would cut at that volume and wall, **in the Asian order of section 0**. k_hole = 1.0 (the kernel's prior). A ratio under 1 means the maker's hole is smaller than the kernel's.

## 3. The window throat: what a cut is worth

The kernel takes the window as a prism through the wall: G_w = A / (t + k·d_eq), with t the wall at the window. For the 80 cm³ window (A = 62.84 mm², d_eq = 8.94 mm, k = 0.80) the wall of 4 mm is 36 % of the effective length.

| Effective throat depth t, mm | G_w, mm | Against t = 4 mm | A4 moves by, cents (same window, same volume) | Volume the same window tunes to A4, cm³ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2.0 | 6.86 | +21.8 % | +171 | 97 |
| 2.5 | 6.51 | +15.5 % | +125 | 92 |
| 3.0 | 6.19 | +9.8 % | +81 | 88 |
| 3.5 | 5.90 | +4.7 % | +40 | 84 |
| 4.0 | 5.63 | +0.0 % | +0 | 80 |
| 5.0 | 5.17 | -8.2 % | -74 | 73 |
| 6.0 | 4.78 | -15.2 % | -143 | 68 |

A cut that opens the throat acts like a shorter throat. A duct estimate, from the volume each cut removes (notes, open problem 24; all on the 80 cm³ window through a 4 mm wall): take the area as growing evenly from the window outline to the outer face, so that the mean area is volume / 4 mm, and integrate the resistance of that duct. It treats the whole removed volume as duct, which the ramp side is not, so it overstates the effect; the differences between the cuts are the point.

| Cut | Volume removed, mm³ | Mean area / window area | Duct-equivalent depth t, mm | G_w against the plain prism | A4 against the fan cut, cents |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Plain prism (the kernel's model) | 251 | 1.00 | 4.00 | +0 % | -166 |
| Fan (default; the Stage 1 stubs) | 548 | 2.18 | 2.05 | +21 % | +0 |
| Ellipse P1 (+4 mm, shelf 50°) | 474 | 1.89 | 2.30 | +18 % | -23 |
| Ellipse P3 (+3 mm, shelf 40°) | 458 | 1.82 | 2.37 | +17 % | -29 |

The windway turns about the lip edge. With the window 9.65 mm long and the windway 30 mm long:

| Lowered by | Exit moves toward the chamber, mm | Mouth end moves, mm | Jet meets the flat under the lip at |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1.0° | 0.17 | 0.69 | 1.0° from below |
| 2.5° | 0.42 | 1.73 | 2.5° from below |
| 2.7° | 0.46 | 1.87 | 2.7° from below |
| 4.0° | 0.67 | 2.77 | 4.0° from below |
| 10.6° | 1.81 | 7.42 | 10.6° from below |

10.6° is the angle of the owner's sample (Window_cutout.md §10.1), which has a 5.5 mm wall and a flat face inside.

## 5. The windway as a slot

Laminar loss in a slot whose height tapers evenly: Δp = 6 μ L q (h₁ + h₂) / (h₁² h₂²), with q the flow per unit width (jet speed × exit height). Entrance losses are left out, so the real loss is higher. The mouth pressure a manometer reads is the jet's dynamic pressure plus this loss.

| Slot | Length mm | Height, mouth → exit, mm | Loss at a 15 m/s jet (135 Pa) | Loss at a 25 m/s jet (370 Pa) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Kernel rule (taper 1.3) | 30 | 1.56 → 1.20 | 47 Pa (36 % of the jet's) | 79 Pa (21 % of the jet's) |
| Owner's sample wind cut (tapered part) | 23 | 3.00 → 1.30 | 14 Pa (11 % of the jet's) | 23 Pa (6 % of the jet's) |
| Miracle (entrance 2.5–3 mm; exit assumed 1.2) | 31 | 2.75 → 1.20 | 22 Pa (17 % of the jet's) | 37 Pa (10 % of the jet's) |
| Kernel exit with a 3 mm mouth end | 30 | 3.00 → 1.20 | 19 Pa (15 % of the jet's) | 32 Pa (9 % of the jet's) |
| Kernel rule at 45 mm | 45 | 1.56 → 1.20 | 71 Pa (53 % of the jet's) | 118 Pa (32 % of the jet's) |
